title: One guard. Two attack surfaces.
label: LAB DEMONSTRATION
narration: A developer's AI agent browses the web. One hidden line tells it to leak a secret. A founder ships an AI-generated site with holes nobody checked. Sentinel X guards both, and shows its evidence. These demonstrations use our own lab targets.

title: Hostile instructions meet a real gate.
label: SIMULATED AGENT / ACTUAL SDK EXECUTION
narration: Here, the offline agent follows a hostile page instruction. The SDK blocks its off-scope send with HOST NOT ALLOWED, while the legitimate task completes. Monitor mode reports what would have been blocked. These are actual command results, using stubbed tools, not a live browsing model.

title: Small results. Visible denominators.
label: SIMULATED + HISTORICAL OBSERVED
narration: Stored simulation results show fifteen of fifteen attacks blocked, with zero false blocks across eighty-one benign actions. There were still false confirmations. In a tiny recorded muse-glimmer sample, attacks succeeded twice in five unprotected runs, versus zero in four gated runs. This is not statistically conclusive.

title: Findings need a fresh-session re-check.
eyebrow: SITE GUARD / FRESH NODE LAB SCAN
label: OBSERVED / INDEPENDENT RE-CHECK
narration: Now a real scanner runs against our vulnerable Node lab. Findings include evidence identifiers and fresh-session verification. The historical scoring found six of ten planted weaknesses, missing stored cross-site scripting and other classes. Today's coverage differs, as shown. Coverage is not vulnerability recall.

title: A patch proposal is not a fix.
label: VERIFIED CHECKS / HISTORICAL RECORD
narration: The stored fix report records two of eight proposals passing independent checks, still awaiting approval. Six escalated to a human. This rejected candidate failed its actual Git application check. No patch is silently deployed. PHP verification shown here is historical; Docker is unavailable for this recording.

title: Approval. Activation. Actual HTTP enforcement.
label: OBSERVED / TEMPORARY SHIELD, NOT A FIX
narration: Shield uses a real local API, a separate proxy, and a synthetic upstream. We propose a narrow rule, record operator approval, then activate it. The matching request receives HTTP four-oh-three. The upstream receives nothing. Benign health traffic gets two hundred. Removing the rule restores forwarding. The measured activation time is on screen.

title: Protection has boundaries.
label: OBSERVED / HISTORICAL LAB REPLAY
narration: The historical replay blocked thirty-eight of sixty-five attacker requests, with zero of forty benign requests blocked. Benign clients were outside the attacker-scoped rules, so this is no general false-positive guarantee. Injection remained unprotected. Intent labels were weak. Human escalation is part of the design, not a hidden failure.

title: Models propose. Independent checks decide.
label: OBSERVED + VERIFIED CHAIN CHECK
narration: Shared evidence separates attempted actions from executed actions. A fresh hash-chain test verifies clean records, then detects tampering. Historical report databases are absent here and honestly marked NO DB. Models explain and propose; deterministic policy and independent verification decide.

title: For agent builders and small teams.
label: NO NEW MODEL CALLS IN THIS DEMO
narration: Start with the CLI or Python SDK. Meta model integrations use NVIDIA and Baseten. Model-backed results shown are recorded evidence; this video makes no new provider calls.

title: Sentinel X
label: LAB-ONLY PROTOTYPE / HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED
narration: For agent builders, solo founders, and small teams: test before trusting. Lab-only scope, incomplete coverage, tiny model samples, and a temporary shield. Explore the code, reproduce the evidence, and review the limitations. Sentinel X.
